paper_design_summary: The analyzed sample consists of 331 U.S. Prolific workers with design, marketing, or product experience who developed a marketing-campaign plan with a GPT-4o chat assistant after psychometric measures and an AI-guided interview. Individuals were randomly assigned to generic, personalized-to-self, or personalized-to-another-person assistance, with no unassisted arm. Campaigns were evaluated for quality, semantic distinctiveness relative to the pooled campaign centroid, and content/length; expert-human quality ratings validated a campaign subset, and a separate AI-only benchmark reused the human-AI campaigns.

studies.label: Marketing-campaign experiment (generic vs personalized vs partially personalized GPT-4o assistant)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Configuration of the GPT-4o assistant used to write the campaign: generic, fully personalized (own profile), or partially personalized (another participant's profile)
assignment.quote: In this study, we randomly assigned 331 subjects to work with either a personalized, partially personalized, or generic AI assistant and then tasked them to develop a marketing plan for a fictional startup.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 5, Introduction; pp. 21-22, Experimental Design. The 331 is the analyzed sample per p. 19; pre-exclusion assignment counts are not stated.
assignment.prereg_locator: PDF p. 19, Participants: 'We re-registered our study design and primary analyses'; embedded hyperlink https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/QF3G7. The saved document supplies neither a registration date nor its timing relative to data collection. The linked protocol and prespecified outcome hierarchy have not been independently verified; the affirmative preregistration flag is therefore unsupported. Random assignment is separately explicit on PDF p. 5.

arms.name: Generic AI
arms.description: GPT-4o (temperature 1) assistant prompted to ask focused questions, build on the person's contributions, and give feedback; given company description and initial campaign idea; no personal information

arms.name: Personalized AI
arms.description: Same generic GPT-4o prompt plus a synthesis of the participant's creativity incorporating cognitive, psychological, and demographic traits, and a summary of their AI-guided interview on marketing experience and work style (PDF pp. 21-22, 38).

arms.name: Partially personalized AI
arms.description: Same personalized prompt, but filled with the profile and interview summary of another participant in the study

participants.exclusions: PDF p. 19 reports 461 recruited; 12 excluded for failing at least 1 of 2 attention checks, 65 for using another AI tool, 42 for not engaging with the interview chatbot and task assistant, and 11 for completing the study in under 30 minutes. The remaining 331 and arm sizes 116/114/101 are post-exclusion analysis counts, despite being called randomized in the prose. Counts assigned before exclusions, and exclusions by arm, are not stated; several exclusions concern behavior during the task. PDF p. 18 instead says 331 recruited; use the explicit recruitment/exclusion flow on p. 19. No intention-to-treat claim is made here.
participants.who: U.S. Prolific workers with at least 99% prior-task approval and self-reported experience in design/creative work, marketing, or product management; mean age 38.7 years, 49.8% female, 73.1% with at least a bachelor's degree; 31.1% marketing experts, 34.1% product experts, 34.7% neither (PDF pp. 18-19).
participants.quote: After applying these exclusion criteria, a sample of 331 individuals was brought forward for analysis with 116 participants randomized to generic AI, 114 to personalized AI, and 101 to partially personalized AI (Table S2).
participants.locator: PDF pp. 18-19, Participants; PDF p. 52 (supplement p. 24), Table S2.

ai_tool.how_used: Open chat while developing the campaign; assistant prompted to ask focused questions, build on contributions, give feedback, and deliver the final brief when requested. Both personalized arms add profile/interview information to the generic prompt; partial personalization uses another participant's profile (PDF pp. 21-22, 37-38). No guidance on interacting with the assistant was provided (p. 17). Participants sent a mean of 5.8 messages (SD 4.5, range 1-20; p. 19).

task.description: Develop a 300-400-word marketing-campaign plan for Cultivated, a fictional lab-grown ribeye startup. Required components: context/product positioning, target audience, messaging/trust building, channel/experience strategy, and success metrics; an initial idea was optional inspiration (PDF p. 21). Coded as idea_generation because the requested artifact is a marketing strategy/plan, rather than advertising copy alone (p. 5; Fig. 1 task panel, p. 8).
task.duration: Methods: approximately 45 minutes for the whole study (PDF p. 18); at least 5 minutes requested for the campaign with no maximum imposed, observed mean 18.9 minutes (SD 14.7; p. 21). Fig. 1 task-panel wording instead gives an estimated 2 hours (p. 8); the document does not explain this discrepant estimate.

outcomes.name: Campaign quality, LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini, rubric score 1-10)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-4o-mini (temperature 0) scores each submitted campaign on overall quality and likely effectiveness from 1 to 10; rubric covers strategic positioning, messaging/trust building, and tactical feasibility, with creativity among its criteria (PDF pp. 23, 39). Coded usefulness, not a dedicated overall-creativity rating. OLS controls for message/turn count; one campaign is the scored observation. Robustness variants remain within this outcome: average of 4 small LLM judges, Personalized 0.35 (0.16)* and Partial 0.34 (0.16)*; average of 3 large judges, Personalized 0.36 (0.18)* and Partial 0.26 (0.17) (Table S3, PDF p. 59). Table S4 (values p. 59, caption p. 60): simplified 1-5 criteria, Personalized 0.10 (0.07), Partial 0.10 (0.07); different-company placebo, 0.09 (0.14) and 0.01 (0.14); unrelated-task placebo, -0.04 (0.06) and -0.08 (0.06); modified criteria, 0.50 (0.19)** and 0.44 (0.19)*. LLM pairwise Elo: Personalized beta = 79.7, SE = 35.4, p = 0.02 in Fig. S2B caption (p. 53), but p = 0.03 in main p. 7 and supplement p. 4 (PDF p. 32); Partial beta = 38.6, SE = 34.4, p = 0.26 (p. 54). The exact personalized Elo p-value is unresolved; both printed versions are retained. Skills-interaction model: Personalized beta = 2.4, SE = 1.1, p = 0.03; Partial beta = 1.4, SE = 1.1, p = 0.21 (Fig. 2A, p. 9). The paper calls the LLM rating its primary metric (p. 7) and selects LLM ratings for primary analyses (p. 33).

contrasts.reported: Personalized beta = 0.59, SE = 0.21, p = 0.005 (main text). Table S3: Personalized 0.59 (0.21)**, Generic reference, controlling for Turn Count 0.06 (0.02)**. Arm means and SDs are not reported. Skills-interaction and alternative-rating models are described in measure_detail.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 6, Results; PDF p. 59 (supplement p. 31), Table S3.

contrasts.reported: Table S3: Partial Personalization 0.56 (0.21)** versus Generic. This main quality contrast is positive; the different skills-interaction model reports beta = 1.4, SE = 1.1, p = 0.21 and is described as no difference. These are distinct specifications, not opposite effect directions.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 59 (supplement p. 31), Table S3; PDF pp. 7, 9, Results and Fig. 2A.

outcomes.name: Campaign quality, human expert pairwise Elo (validation subsample)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Expert-human pairwise Elo quality validation: 200 U.S. Prolific raters working in upper/middle management, consulting, or market research each made 10 pairwise comparisons of overall quality. A random subset of 100 campaigns came only from Generic and Personalized AI; mean 39.6 ratings per campaign, range 26-55; initial Elo 1500, K-factor 32 (PDF p. 32). Human/LLM Elo correlation r = 0.72, p < 0.001 (p. 33). One final campaign Elo score is the analysis unit; raters are not additional experimental participants, and the 100-campaign arm split is not stated.

contrasts.reported: No significant treatment difference: beta = 158.2, p = 0.14, directionally higher for personalized AI. No SE or arm split is printed. Marketing-skills covariate: beta = 22.2, p = 0.01; this is not an AI treatment effect.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 32 (supplement p. 4), Sensitivity Analyses; validation correlation continues on p. 33.

outcomes.name: Campaign theme diversity relative to the pooled campaign centroid (paper: creativity)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-4o extracts distinctive campaign themes of 1-3 words; text-embedding-3-large embeds those themes. The paper defines the score through cosine similarity to the mean embedding of all campaigns across treatment conditions (PDF p. 23; extraction prompt p. 40), and interprets higher reported creativity scores as less homogeneity (p. 10). The transformation from cosine similarity to the printed creativity scale is not given. Coded diversity/across_people because the reference is other participants' outputs; a pooled reference centroid does not measure within-arm dispersion alone. All-sample means are kept separate from post-treatment quality-tertile contrasts. Rubric tertiles are low <7/10, medium 7/10, high 8/10 (p. 23); LLM-Elo tertiles are a robustness variant (Fig. S2C, pp. 53-54). Subgroup sample sizes are not printed. Primary versus secondary status for this measure is not explicitly stated.

contrasts.reported: Full sample: Personalized Creativity_mean = 52.3, 95% CI [46.8, 57.8]; Generic = 53.7, 95% CI [48.2, 59.2]. No full-sample Personalized-versus-Generic contrast test is printed; no_clear_difference records this lack of a demonstrated contrast, not a tested null effect.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10, Personalization as Pathway to Counteract AI-Based Homogenization.

contrasts.reported: Full sample: Partially personalized Creativity_mean = 56.5, 95% CI [51.0, 62.1]; Generic = 53.7, 95% CI [48.2, 59.2]. No full-sample Partial-versus-Generic contrast test is printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10, Personalization as Pathway to Counteract AI-Based Homogenization.

diversity_detail.metric: Theme similarity to the pooled centroid, reported on an unspecified creativity scale where higher means less similarity/more diversity.
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each campaign's extracted themes versus the average embedding of all campaigns across treatment conditions (PDF p. 23). The centroid pools arms; the paper does not state whether AI-only benchmark campaigns enter it.
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Arm means and 95% CIs (p. 10); subgroup regression coefficients/SEs/p-values in Fig. 2B and Fig. S2C. The CI calculation and handling of dependence through the common centroid are not described; a full-sample treatment contrast test is not printed.
diversity_detail.notes: Neither screener's within-arm-centroid requirement appears in the codebook. This measure compares outputs across participants, so it is coded diversity/across_people; it should not be interpreted as a pure within-condition dispersion estimate. Printed creativity already increases with diversity, so no sign was reversed and no effect was calculated.

eligibility.reason: S1 meets all three criteria: individual random assignment to generic, personalized, or partially personalized generative-AI assistance (PDF p. 5; pp. 21-22, Experimental Design); 331 people analyzed after exclusions, with Generic 116, Personalized 114, and Partial 101 (PDF p. 19; Table S2, p. 52); and quality ratings plus cross-campaign theme similarity scored on participants' submitted campaigns (PDF pp. 22-23, 39-40). GPT-4o was available during campaign production (p. 21). Different AI configurations qualify under the codebook without a Human Only arm. Pre-exclusion assignment counts and preregistration timing are unknown, but neither uncertainty changes these documented criteria. S2 is a non-randomized AI-only versus human-AI benchmark that reuses S1 outputs and supplies no additional eligible sample. The word-count measure category is null; eligibility is independently established by S1-O1 and S1-O3.

one_line_finding: Personalized versus generic GPT-4o increased LLM-rated campaign quality (beta = 0.59, SE = 0.21, p = 0.005; PDF p. 6, Table S3 p. 59), while higher theme diversity was reported within the top quality tertile (beta = 20.5, SE = 6.5, p = 0.002; Fig. 2B p. 9), with no full-sample diversity contrast test printed.
open_questions: The exact version and posting date of the saved undated arXiv PDF remain unidentified; its creation metadata is not a publication date. Authors could identify the matching manuscript version. This concerns provenance, not an eligibility criterion.

The PDF only says the study design and primary analyses were re-registered (p. 19). Registration timing relative to data collection, protocol content, and prespecified outcome hierarchy remain unverified. Authors could supply the dated protocol and data-collection timeline. Preregistration is not an eligibility requirement.

Pre-exclusion randomization totals and arm-specific exclusions are not given (PDF p. 19). Authors' allocation and exclusion records would settle these counts. The confirmed 331 analyzed people already satisfy criterion 2.

The creativity-score transformation, arm-CI method, and whether AI-only campaigns enter the pooled centroid are not stated (PDF pp. 10, 23). Posted analysis code would settle these details; the cross-participant output measure already establishes criterion 3.

Personalized LLM Elo p = 0.03 in main p. 7 and supplement p. 4 (PDF p. 32), versus p = 0.02 in Fig. S2B (PDF p. 53). Matching posted analysis code/model output would resolve the exact p-value. This duplicates an unresolved reconciliation difference and does not affect eligibility.

The reference group/model for the AI-only beta = -21.9 is not explicitly identified (PDF p. 10). Posted analysis code/model output would identify the reference. This duplicates an unresolved reconciliation difference and concerns S2, not the eligible S1 sample.

The Fig. 1 task panel gives an estimated 2 hours (PDF p. 8), whereas Methods describes an approximately 45-minute study (p. 18), with no maximum on the campaign task (p. 21). Authors could confirm the instructions actually deployed. This duplicates an unresolved reconciliation difference and does not affect eligibility.

Ordinary campaign word count has no exact supported measure category in the current codebook; measure is null. Its output-length method is established by PDF pp. 19 and 61. No additional paper source is needed; a codebook mapping decision is required, and criterion 3 is independently met by other outcomes.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-09 after reading the entire markdown conversion and checking the relevant PDF pages, tables, embedded links, and figure panels. All page locators are PDF pages; supplement page k is PDF page 28+k. Both raw forms parsed. There is one independent human experimental sample; expert raters, simulated campaigns, and the reused S2 comparator are not added to its 331 people. Campaigns are the scored observations; in S1 each participant submits one campaign, so those output and participant counts coincide, but no participant-aggregated outcome is described. Both screeners' novelty/with_ai coding of pooled theme similarity was corrected to diversity/across_people under the codebook. Full-sample diversity means are descriptive, not evidence of a tested null effect; high/medium quality subgroups condition on a treatment-affected score. The main quality regression also controls for treatment-affected message count. Campaign completeness and marketing-term count were omitted by both screeners but are output-scored indicators retained without invented treatment effects. Word-count is retained from B. Self-reported assistance/trust, conversational turns and AI-response embedding shifts, and differences between a person's final campaign and their own AI draft are process measures rather than creativity/diversity across people; baseline DAT/AUT measures preceded AI assignment. They are not listed as creativity outcomes. The separate pre-study prompt-bias simulations and personalization-response simulations have no eligible human outcome and are described only as methodological checks, not additional eligible studies. AI-only versus human-AI is coded other, rather than the codebook's unaided ai_vs_human class. The manuscript's rubric and Elo definitions of high quality explain its all-versus-approximately-80% AI-only descriptions. Fig. 2A's panel label differs from the interaction coefficient in its caption; the form records the caption/text specification, not a value inferred from the graph. No effect sizes, subgroup counts, arm SDs, or uncertainty estimates were calculated. Finalized on 2026-10-09 after reading all 151997 characters of the saved markdown, including the complete supplement, and independently checking the PDF eligibility passages, numerical results, tables, links, and relevant figure panels. Two challenge problems were corrected: preregistration is not_stated, and plain word count has measure null because the vocabulary has no supported exact category. The requested across_people label for S2 was rejected under the form specification's explicit none rule for comparisons outside the human-assistance questions. All original open questions and the three unresolved reconciliation differences are addressed in final.open_items; none affects eligibility. The existing supplement record is complete. S1 remains online_rct; S2 is a benchmark within this paper, not a reanalysis of another paper's randomized experiment. The reconciliation object is preserved unchanged as the prior review record; final records the later adjudications.

open_items.item: Saved PDF version/posting date remains unidentified (original open_questions[0]; source.version). Authors could identify the matching manuscript and its posting history; creation metadata is insufficient. Provenance only.

Registration timing, protocol content, and prespecified outcome hierarchy remain unverified (original open_questions[0]; PDF p. 19; assignment challenge). Authors could supply the dated protocol and data-collection timeline. Preregistration is not one of the three criteria.

Pre-exclusion allocation totals and exclusions by arm are unknown (original open_questions[1]; PDF p. 19). Authors' allocation/exclusion logs would resolve them; 331 analyzed people are independently confirmed for criterion 2.

Creativity transformation, arm-CI procedure, and inclusion of AI-only campaigns in the pooled centroid remain unspecified (original open_questions[2]; PDF pp. 10, 23). Posted scoring/analysis code would settle them. The output-based cross-participant measure already establishes criterion 3.

Personalized LLM Elo p = 0.03 in text versus 0.02 in Fig. S2B remains unresolved (original open_questions[3]; PDF pp. 7, 32, 53; unresolved reconciliation difference for S1-O1.measure_detail). Matching analysis code/model output would settle the exact p-value; statistical significance is not an eligibility criterion.

The reference group/model for AI-only beta = -21.9 remains unstated (original open_questions[4]; PDF p. 10; unresolved reconciliation difference for the benchmark contrast). Posted model formula/output would identify it. S1 eligibility is independent of S2.

Fig. 1's estimated 2 hours versus the approximately 45-minute study and unrestricted campaign duration remains unexplained (original open_questions[5]; PDF pp. 8, 18, 21; unresolved reconciliation difference for task.duration). Authors could identify the deployed instructions. No criterion requires a particular task duration.

Plain campaign word count has no exact supported codebook measure category; measure is null (S1-O4; PDF pp. 19, 61). The source method is settled, so no additional paper material is needed; only a codebook mapping decision remains. Other output outcomes independently meet criterion 3.
